sources.citation: Sol Dourdin T, Rivière G, Cormier A, Di Poi C, Guyomard K, Rabiller M, Akcha F, Bah TS, Le Monier P, Sussarellu R (2023). Molecular and phenotypic effects of early exposure to an environmentally relevant pesticide mixture in the Pacific oyster, Crassostrea gigas. Environmental Pollution 326:121472.
sources.read: Full text of the accepted author version (Ifremer Archimer 00829/94090), including methods, results, discussion and figure captions. The supplement (tab. SM1-SM5, fig. SM1-SM4, incl. the DMG list tab. SM4 and the cross-stage DMG table SM5) was not obtained, so no gene-level methylation claims could be taken from P1.
sources.libraries: F0: gastrula (6 hpf) and metamorphosis-competent pediveliger (MCP, 19 dpf) libraries; exposure 0-48 hpf, control vs exposed. The paper analysed 10 gastrula libraries (4 control, 6 exposed; control tank C1 dropped for arrested development) and 12 MCP libraries (6 and 6).

sources.citation: Sol Dourdin T, Guyomard K, Rabiller M, Houssais N, Cormier A, Le Monier P, Sussarellu R, Rivière G (2024). Ancestors' Gift: Parental Early Exposure to the Environmentally Realistic Pesticide Mixture Drives Offspring Phenotype in a Larger Extent Than Direct Exposure in the Pacific Oyster, Crassostrea gigas. Environmental Science & Technology 58(4):1865-1876.
sources.read: Full text of the accepted author version (Ifremer Archimer 00872/98346), including the SI figure captions and the SI variant-splicing note bundled in that PDF; SI workbook es3c08201_si_002.xlsx from figshare 24994504 (Tables SI3-SI7 read: DEG lists, interaction genes, DMR/DMG counts, interaction DMGs, DMG-and-DEG genes).
sources.libraries: F1: CC, CE, EC, EE (first letter = parental F0 treatment, second = F1 exposure 0-48 hpf), 3 gastrula and 3 MCP (16 dpf) libraries each.

caveats: The sample sheet has no separate columns for stage, generation and exposure, so no factors are registered and every differential claim waits for them; the claims carry the factor names they will use (stage, generation, exposure, parental_exposure).

claims.where: Abstract; Highlights; Discussion (demethylation trend, 77.1% of DMCs hypo in MCP larvae)
claims.statement: Early pesticide-mixture exposure significantly changed DNA methylation in F0 MCP larvae 17 days after exposure ended, with a demethylation trend: 77.1% of the 220 DMCs were hypomethylated in exposed larvae.
claims.re_derived: Exposure factor not registered. Once registered, test as dm_direction on exposure E vs T within F0 pediveliger; paper's unit is DMCs (per-CpG), ours would be genes.

claims.where: Discussion (60.7% of DMCs hypo in gastrulae); Highlights
claims.statement: In F0 gastrulae (6 h of exposure) the methylation differences also leaned to hypomethylation: 60.7% of DMCs were hypomethylated in exposed embryos.
claims.re_derived: Exposure factor not registered. Once registered, dm_direction on exposure E vs T within F0 gastrula; per-CpG unit in the paper.

claims.statement: Exposed F0 oysters show a global DNA demethylation during (gastrula) and after (MCP larva) the exposure window, i.e. lower methylation in exposed than in control animals; the paper supports this only with DMC direction, not with a reported global level.
claims.re_derived: Exposure factor not registered. Once registered, test as group_difference of overall CpG methylation per library, exposed lower than control, within F0 gastrula and F0 pediveliger separately. No numeric global levels are given in the paper.

claims.statement: Exposure produced 507 DMCs in F0 gastrulae (methylKit, difference >= 25%, q < 0.01, min depth 10).
claims.re_derived: Per-CpG counts; also exposure factor not registered. Gene-level analogue is C6.

claims.statement: Exposure produced 220 DMCs in F0 MCP larvae (same methylKit thresholds).
claims.re_derived: Per-CpG counts; also exposure factor not registered. Gene-level analogue is C7.

claims.statement: 386 genes in F0 gastrulae contained at least one DMC; 147 contained hypermethylated and 227 hypomethylated cytosines.
claims.re_derived: Exposure factor not registered. A 'gene with >=1 DMC' is not the same as a gene significant in a per-gene model, so expect only order-of-magnitude comparability.

claims.statement: 175 genes in F0 MCP larvae contained at least one DMC; 40 with hypermethylated and 135 with hypomethylated cytosines.
claims.re_derived: Exposure factor not registered.

claims.statement: Among F0 gastrula DMGs, hypomethylated genes outnumber hypermethylated ones (227 vs 147, about 61% hypo).
claims.re_derived: Exposure factor not registered.

claims.statement: Among F0 MCP-larva DMGs, hypomethylated genes dominate (135 vs 40, about 77% hypo).
claims.re_derived: Exposure factor not registered.

claims.statement: About 70% of methylated CpGs in control F0 gastrulae and MCP larvae lie in gene bodies.
claims.re_derived: Share of methylated CpGs by genomic feature; we have per-gene sums, not per-CpG feature annotation. It is consistent with, but does not state, gene bodies being more methylated than promoters or genome.

claims.statement: Most DMCs fall in genes (promoters, exons or introns): 75% in gastrulae and 84% in MCP larvae.
claims.re_derived: Per-DMC feature annotation.

claims.statement: Relative to the distribution of methylated CpGs, DMCs are over-represented in intergenic regions in gastrulae, and in intergenic regions and introns in MCP larvae (chi-squared p < 0.0001).
claims.re_derived: Needs intergenic and intron partitions and per-CpG calls.

claims.statement: 18 of the 175 MCP-larva DMGs were already DMGs in gastrulae; 10 of them kept the same direction and 15 of 18 were hypomethylated in MCP larvae.
claims.re_derived: Exposure factor not registered, and tab. SM5 (gene identities) was not obtained.

claims.statement: GO analysis found no enriched terms among DMGs at either stage.
claims.re_derived: Enrichment analysis not in our outputs.

claims.statement: RNA-seq of F0 gastrulae found 14 DEGs between exposed and control (10 down, 4 up in exposed), including developmental transcription factors such as Pax6, Elf-2, goosecoid and engrailed-like; no DEGs in MCP larvae.
claims.re_derived: Expression claim (DESeq2, |log2FC| > 0.5, padj < 0.05).

claims.statement: Differential methylation and differential expression were not correlated in F0.
claims.re_derived: Requires expression data.

claims.statement: Exposure had no effect on 24 hpf larval abnormality (82.5% vs 82.6% normal) or gastrula DNA strand breaks, but exposed larvae were less mobile and slower at 8 dpf, and exposed MCP larvae had a lower epinephrine-induced metamorphosis rate (23.6% vs 30.3%).
claims.re_derived: Phenotypic endpoints; not measured by the methylation pipeline.

claims.statement: Exposed F0 animals were transiently longer as larvae and heavier as spat (2-4 months), and had 9.5% higher field survival than controls (log-rank p = 0.0003).
claims.re_derived: Phenotypic endpoints; not measured by the methylation pipeline.

claims.statement: In F1 gastrulae, overall methylation separated samples by parental (F0) treatment along PC1, which explained 89.75% of the variance (PCA of the 1000 most variable 500 bp tiles).
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered. Once registered, test as clustering on F1 gastrula samples only; our PCA is on gene-body methylation (and across all samples unless subset), the paper's on tiles.

claims.statement: In F1 MCP larvae, overall methylation did not separate samples by either parental (F0) or own (F1) treatment on the PCA.
claims.re_derived: Factors not registered. A null clustering claim: once registered, check that neither parental_exposure nor exposure separates F1 pediveliger samples on PC1/PC2.

claims.statement: F1 gastrulae from exposed vs control parents differed at 4349 DMRs (500 bp tiles, Wald p < 0.05, |difference| >= 10%).
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered; also region-level (tiles) rather than genes, see C23 for the gene count.

claims.statement: In F1 gastrulae, offspring of exposed parents were mostly hypermethylated: 3914 of 4349 DMRs (90%) hyper, 435 hypo.
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered.

claims.statement: The F1 gastrula lineage DMRs intersected 2345 genes (2098 with hyper- and 247 with hypomethylated DMRs).
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered. Genes overlapping >=1 DMR, not per-gene tests.

claims.statement: 89.5% of F1 gastrula lineage DMGs were hypermethylated in offspring of exposed parents.
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered.

claims.statement: F1 MCP larvae from exposed vs control parents differed at 550 DMRs (372 hyper, 178 hypo; 67.6% hyper).
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered; region-level unit.

claims.statement: The F1 MCP-larva lineage DMRs intersected 337 genes (232 hyper, 105 hypo).
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered.

claims.statement: 68.8% of F1 MCP-larva lineage DMGs were hypermethylated in offspring of exposed parents (a hypermethylation trend at both F1 stages).
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered.

claims.where: Tab. SI7 (genes both differentially methylated and expressed in gastrulae, with mean DMR difference)
claims.statement: Named genes differentially methylated between F1 gastrula lineages (and also differentially expressed) include integrin alpha-4, LRP6, MRP1, ADAMTS16, CEBPD and NR0B1, nearly all hypermethylated in the exposed lineage (directions from the sign of mean_Diff, assumed exposed minus control).
claims.re_derived: parental_exposure not registered. Paper IDs are GCA_902806645.1 gene models (G-numbers); match by product description. 'Gene' here means DMR overlapping gene coordinates, taken as gene_body.

claims.where: Results 3.5; Tab. SI5, SI6; Fig. SI10
claims.statement: Methylation showed F1-by-F0 treatment interactions: 103 DMRs in 84 genes in gastrulae and 141 DMRs in 69 genes in MCP larvae (LRT p < 0.1).
claims.re_derived: Interaction contrast (parental_exposure x exposure) is not part of our single-factor contrasts, and neither factor is registered.

claims.statement: F1 gastrula lineage DMRs were over-represented in intergenic regions, which hold 15% of constitutive methylation but 27% of DMRs (chi-squared p < 0.05).
claims.re_derived: Needs an intergenic partition and region-level calls.

claims.statement: Pesticide-associated differential methylation went in opposite directions across generations: hypomethylation in exposed F0 (P1) versus hypermethylation in F1 offspring of exposed parents.
claims.re_derived: Joint statement over C1/C2 (F0 exposure, hypo) and C22/C24/C27 (F1 parental exposure, hyper); testable only by combining those once factors are registered.

claims.statement: In F1 gastrulae, 51 genes were both differentially methylated and expressed with no correlation between the two, and a PLS showed methylation (first latent component, 66.1% of variance, separating CC from EE) as the main driver; no PLS separation in MCP larvae, and no DMG was a DEG at that stage.
claims.re_derived: Integration with expression data.

claims.statement: Parental exposure changed F1 gene expression (451 DEGs in gastrulae, 241 in MCP larvae), with F1:F0 interaction genes such as calmodulin, MyD88 and OLIG3 in gastrulae and HSP68/HSP70 in MCP larvae, and lower expression of calmodulin and two adrenergic receptors in MCP larvae from exposed parents.
claims.re_derived: Expression claims.

claims.statement: Transcriptomic response to pesticide exposure in F1 MCP larvae was significant in the control lineage but attenuated in the exposed lineage (MCMCglmm p = 0.006 vs n.s.).
claims.re_derived: Expression-based DAPC.

claims.statement: SNP allele frequencies show similar genetic divergence between F1 lineages (AFD 0.079) as between parents and offspring, but SNPs overlap only 6% of gastrula DMRs and 0% of MCP DMRs, so methylation differences are argued to be largely independent of genetic divergence.
claims.re_derived: Genotype analysis from RNA-seq SNPs and DMR coordinates.

claims.statement: Parental exposure mattered more for F1 phenotype than own exposure: the exposed lineage had a lower epinephrine-induced metamorphosis rate (F1 exposure also lowered it, no interaction), and EE spat had lower field survival (24%) than CC, CE and EC (33%, 32%, 32%).
claims.re_derived: Phenotypic endpoints.

claims.statement: Lineage DMGs were enriched for cell fate, cell junction and muscle development terms in gastrulae, and for development and organismal homeostasis terms in MCP larvae.
claims.re_derived: GO enrichment not in our outputs.
